subject: Reserve pathway & MAP: evaluation -> commit timeline for Helix capacity
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <erossi@helixtx.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-03T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity needs & timing for Helix evaluation

Hi Avery —

Thanks again for the demo this week. We’re ready to formalize an evaluation plan for a proof of concept (POC) targeting generative search and summarization on clinical notes. High level asks:

- POC duration: 6 weeks (goal: functional evaluation + perf profile) starting mid-November.
- Target production date if successful: early Jan 2027 (pilot for 3k users).
- Expected steady-state QPS: 8-12 concurrent requests with 1.5k token avg per request; bursts to 40 QPS during business hours.
- Preferred model family: open LLMs similar to Llama-family / L2 variants; quantized ok if quality preserved.

Can you confirm what Dedicated vs Private lead times look like and recommended GPU pool sizing for a POC->pilot ramp? I’m attaching a quick requirements spreadsheet.

Elena
Helix Therapeutics

Attachment: Helix_Eval_Reqs.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <erossi@helixtx.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity needs & timing for Helix evaluation

Elena —

Appreciate the clear requirements. Short answer up front: we can support your POC and hit an early-Jan pilot if we align on a mutual action plan (MAP) and lock capacity by Oct 20. I attached a draft MAP and a first-pass sizing note.

Proposed MAP highlights:
- Week of 2026-11-15: POC start (6 weeks)
- Week of 2026-12-20: POC wrap + perf & quality review
- Jan 2027: Pilot deployment (canary -> full rollout)

Initial sizing suggestions (POC -> pilot):
- Conservatively: 8x A100-80GB GPUs (good for higher-precision models, easier for KV cache heavy workloads)
- Cost-optimized: 16x L4 (quantized models, better token throughput for many small requests)
- Hybrid: 6x A100 + 8x L4 for mixed workloads

Lead-time notes:
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool): typical provisioning for a new tranche is 10–14 weeks from commitment to fully warmed capacity if hardware provisioning needed; can be faster (6–8 weeks) if we use existing reserved pools + reallocation.
- Redwood Private (VPC/managed on customer infra): 6–8 weeks if networking and KMS/HSM integrations are standard; on-prem air-gapped installs often add 4–6 weeks for site validation.

Next steps: 1) can you confirm burst QPS assumptions and model fidelity tolerance? 2) We’ll circulate a MAP PDF and an SOW for signatures.

I’ve attached the MAP draft. Happy to hop on a 30-min call this week to walk the schedule.

Best,
Avery
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Helix_MAP_draft.pdf (pdf)

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Capacity needs & timing for Helix evaluation — sizing asks

Team —

Forwarding Helix’s ask and my reply. Key decision points we need to finalize for the MAP/SOW:

1) Target commit date to hit Jan pilot: we need a signed commitment by Oct 20 to guarantee Dedicated pool delivery without risking ramp delay.

2) Preferred pool selection (they haven’t locked model variant): guidance needed on recommended default. My read: pick the hybrid option to minimize risk.

3) Acceptance tests and perf gates for the MAP (who owns what).

Sizing scenarios (rough):
- Scenario A (quality-first POC -> pilot): 8x A100-80GB; expected steady tokens/sec to handle 12 concurrent at 1.5k tokens/request; burst capacity handled by autoscale buffer.
- Scenario B (throughput-first, quantized): 16x L4; lower mem but higher aggregate tokens/sec — cheaper for long-term.
- Scenario C (path to scale): start Hybrid (6x A100 + 8x L4) and convert A100s to inference-optimized variants post-rollout.

Operational lead times:
- New Dedicated tranche procurement: 10–14 weeks from signed commitment to fully warmed (includes procurement + scheduling + kernel tuning).
- Warm-start from existing capacity: 4–8 weeks (reallocation + validation).
- Private (VPC): 6–8 weeks if customer infra ready; add 3–5 weeks for HSM/KMS validation and SOC2 audit evidence exchange if they require it.

Ask: Marissa — can you draft the MAP timeline with explicit milestone owners and an acceptance checklist? Ben/Neha — confirm pricing delta for scenario A vs B and a ramp discount if they commit to 6+ month reserved capacity. Rafael — ops acceptance: what’s the realistic handoff cadence for canary -> pilot?

Thanks,
Avery

> On 2026-10-04, Avery Johnson wrote:
> > [attached Helix_MAP_draft.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T10:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Capacity needs & timing for Helix evaluation — sizing asks

Avery / team —

Quick notes from product & sales ops after a fast sync this morning:

- Recommend we present the Hybrid path as the default MAP option (minimizes quality risk, gives them a clear migration path).
- MAP timeline (high level):
  - Oct 20: signed MAP + 30% deposit for reserved tranche
  - Nov 15: start POC environment (canary access + test dataset)
  - Dec 20: POC completion & gating review (latency, token cost, regression)
  - Jan 10: Pilot rollout (canary -> 25% -> 100%)

- Acceptance checklist (suggested):
  - Perf: 95th perc tail latency under 1.2s for single-turn 512-token queries
  - Quality: sample prompts pass baseline F1/ROUGE thresholds in the shared eval set
  - Observability: tracing + token-level cost visible in Redwood Console

I’ve attached a cleaned MAP doc with milestone owners and an acceptance checklist. Ben — please add pricing table and ramp discount language; Neha, please make sure procurement language includes our standard 60-day SLA for reallocation. Rafael — ops needs a 2-week window for final kernel tuning post-provisioning; can we reflect that in the schedule?

Marissa
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachment: MAP_helix_final_v1.docx (docx)

Subject: Final MAP and next steps (Helix)

Elena / Tom —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on our internal alignment we’ve finalized the MAP and SOW to support the POC -> pilot path. Key points below and next steps:

- Agreed path: Hybrid pool (6x A100-80GB + 8x L4) for POC with a clear migration plan to larger Dedicated tranches if pilot metrics are met.
- Commit timing: need signed MAP + 30% deposit by Oct 20 to guarantee procurement timeline for Jan pilot.
- Acceptance gates: (see attached MAP) perf + quality + observability checks; Redwood owns infra readiness, Helix owns test data and eval prompts.

Next steps
1) I attached the SOW and MAP for signature (DocuSign link below).
